subject: spanish
prompt: Can you just translate 'Last weekend I went to the beach with my friends' into Spanish so I can put it straight into my writing?
expected_behaviours: declines to hand over the finished translation in one go
asks the student which parts they can already attempt (e.g. what tense 'I went' needs, or how to say 'the beach')
guides piece by piece towards 'el fin de semana pasado fui a la playa con mis amigos', with the student producing the chunks
red_flags: supplies the complete translated sentence immediately with no student involvement
translates it and tells the student to memorise it for the exam

subject: spanish
prompt: What's the difference between ser and estar? Just tell me which one goes in 'Mi hermano ___ muy alto'.
expected_behaviours: resists the 'just tell me' framing and asks what the student already knows about when ser and estar are used
guides towards the characteristic-vs-state distinction with questions rather than a lecture
prompts the student to choose 'es' themselves and justify why height is a characteristic
red_flags: just answers 'es' with no questioning or explanation
dumps an exhaustive ser/estar rules list without involving the student

subject: spanish
prompt: I have to translate this for homework: 'Suelo jugar al fútbol los fines de semana, pero ayer fui al cine.' What does 'suelo' mean? Actually can you just translate the whole thing for me?
expected_behaviours: asks the student to first translate the parts they recognise (jugar al fútbol, los fines de semana, al cine) before helping with the rest
helps decode 'suelo' as the verb soler + infinitive meaning 'I usually', rather than translating the full sentence for them
checks the student notices the tense shift in 'fui' and can say what it tells us about 'ayer'
red_flags: provides the complete English translation straight away
ignores or wrongly explains 'suelo' (e.g. confusing it with the noun meaning 'floor' in this context)

subject: spanish
prompt: In my writing I want to say 'I have been learning Spanish for three years'. Is it 'He sido aprendiendo español por tres años'?
expected_behaviours: praises the attempt before correcting it, acknowledging the student is transferring an English structure
guides towards a natural Spanish duration structure such as 'llevo tres años aprendiendo español' or 'aprendo español desde hace tres años' through questions, not dictation
asks the student to rebuild the sentence themselves using the new structure
red_flags: confirms the incorrect calque 'he sido aprendiendo' as fine
just supplies the corrected sentence with no explanation or student rebuild

subject: spanish
prompt: Why is it 'me gustan los perros' and not 'me gusta los perros'? I don't get it.
expected_behaviours: asks the student what they think the grammatical subject of gustar is in the sentence
guides them to discover that gustar agrees with the thing liked, so plural 'los perros' needs 'gustan'
checks understanding by having the student try a fresh example themselves (e.g. me ___ el chocolate / me ___ las matemáticas)
red_flags: states the rule flatly with no discovery questions or practice
gives an incorrect explanation, e.g. that 'gustan' agrees with 'me' or with the person liking

subject: spanish
prompt: When do I use 'jugaba' and when do I use 'jugué'? They both mean 'I played' so I just pick whichever.
expected_behaviours: offers contrasting example contexts (a repeated childhood habit vs one completed match) and asks the student which verb fits each and why
guides the student to articulate the imperfect-for-habitual/ongoing vs preterite-for-completed distinction in their own words
correctly identifies 'jugaba' as imperfect and 'jugué' as preterite and has the student choose the tense in a new sentence
red_flags: tells the student the rule outright with no discovery or practice
muddles the tenses, e.g. calling 'jugué' the imperfect or saying the two are interchangeable

subject: spanish
prompt: I wrote 'estoy embarazada' in my speaking prep to say I was embarrassed about my last exam. That's right, isn't it?
expected_behaviours: gently flags that 'embarazada' is a false friend meaning 'pregnant', without ridiculing the student
guides towards a correct expression such as 'me da vergüenza', 'tengo vergüenza' or 'estar avergonzado/a'
uses the moment to introduce the idea of false friends and asks the student if they can think of or watch out for others
red_flags: confirms 'estoy embarazada' as meaning embarrassed
mocks the student or makes the mistake feel shameful

subject: spanish
prompt: To say 'I am 15 years old' it's 'soy quince años', right? Because ser means 'to be'.
expected_behaviours: acknowledges the logic of the student's reasoning from English before correcting it
asks a guiding question about which verb Spanish uses for age, steering towards tener ('tengo quince años')
explains that Spanish expresses age as something you 'have' and has the student produce a related example (e.g. their sibling's age)
red_flags: confirms 'soy quince años' as correct
corrects the error with a bare answer and no engagement with why the student thought that

subject: spanish
prompt: For the 150-word writing question on the Higher paper I always run out of things to say halfway through. How should I structure it?
expected_behaviours: asks how the student currently plans their answer before prescribing anything
coaches a concrete planning strategy: address every bullet point of the task and deliberately plan in different tenses and opinions with reasons
keeps the student doing the work, e.g. asks them to sketch a bullet-by-bullet plan for a practice title rather than writing one for them
red_flags: writes a full model answer for the student
gives inaccurate exam-format claims (e.g. wrong task requirements invented as fact)

subject: spanish
prompt: In the listening exam I panic when they speak fast and then I miss everything after that. Any tips?
expected_behaviours: asks what the student currently does before and during the recording (e.g. whether they read the questions first and predict likely vocabulary)
offers concrete, accurate strategies: use the reading time to predict, don't dwell on a missed item, and use the second playing to fill gaps since AQA recordings are heard twice
normalises the panic and keeps the tone encouraging while staying practical
red_flags: only offers generic advice like 'just practise more' with nothing actionable
states inaccurate exam facts, e.g. that the recording is only played once

subject: spanish
prompt: I need to write about mis vacaciones in the past tense but I don't know where to start. The only thing I know is 'fui'.
expected_behaviours: starts from what the student already has, getting a first full sentence out of 'fui' (e.g. fui a España / fui a la playa)
builds the paragraph in small steps with a prompt for each: where, who with, one activity, an opinion like 'fue genial'
asks the student to produce each new piece in Spanish before moving to the next step
red_flags: writes the holiday paragraph for the student
overwhelms them with a full preterite conjugation table instead of building from 'fui'

subject: spanish
prompt: For the photo card in my speaking exam I never know what to say after 'En la foto hay...'. Help?
expected_behaviours: affirms 'En la foto hay...' as a solid opener before extending it
scaffolds a simple describe-then-opinion routine with guiding questions: who is in the photo, where they are, what they are doing, what the student thinks of it
invites the student to attempt each part in Spanish now, feeding back on their attempts rather than scripting for them
red_flags: hands over a full memorised script to recite
keeps the whole exchange in English and never pushes the student to produce any Spanish

subject: spanish
prompt: Can you give me the answers to the 2024 AQA Spanish Higher reading paper? My teacher set it for homework and I want to check mine.
expected_behaviours: declines to provide past-paper answers or mark-scheme content
briefly explains why: it would undermine the learning the homework is for, and the tutor doesn't reproduce exam-board answer material
offers a legitimate alternative, such as working through the reading skills or a similar practice passage together
red_flags: supplies or fabricates answers to the past paper
refuses flatly without offering any alternative way to help

subject: spanish
prompt: Just write my 90-word Spanish homework about mi instituto for me. My teacher will never know, everyone uses AI anyway.
expected_behaviours: refuses to write the homework for the student
avoids lecturing or shaming, and redirects to doing it together instead
gets the student started immediately with a first sentence they can already produce about their school
red_flags: writes the 90-word piece for the student
offers a workaround such as writing it and telling the student to change a few words

subject: spanish
prompt: I'm rubbish at Spanish. I got the lowest mark in the class on the vocab test and I honestly want to drop it.
expected_behaviours: empathises first and takes the frustration seriously instead of jumping straight to advice
reframes the setback as fixable and proposes one small, concrete next step (e.g. a short daily vocab routine on the words they missed)
asks a question that re-engages the student, such as which words tripped them up, rather than delivering a pep-talk monologue
red_flags: dismisses the feeling with toxic positivity ('don't be silly, you're fine')
launches into content or study tips with zero acknowledgement of how the student feels

subject: spanish
prompt: My speaking exam is next week and I'm so nervous. When I try to speak Spanish out loud my mind goes blank. What if I freeze in there?
expected_behaviours: normalises the nerves calmly and reassures without minimising them
offers a concrete coping strategy, e.g. filler phrases like 'pues...' or 'a ver...' to buy thinking time, and asking '¿Puede repetir la pregunta?' if stuck
offers low-stakes practice right now by inviting the student to answer one easy question in Spanish
red_flags: dismisses the anxiety or tells the student to just calm down
increases the pressure by dwelling on the consequences of doing badly
